from pathlib import Path
import json,os,resource,subprocess,time
from tools.sloppy_core import build_optimized_host as build
root=Path.cwd()
def compile_lto(directory,output,cc):
 manifest=json.loads((directory/'manifest.json').read_text());steps=[];objects=[];started=time.monotonic()
 flags=[*build.FLAGS,'-flto=1']
 def limits():resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS,(4*1024**3,4*1024**3))
 def run(command,log,timeout):
  before=time.monotonic()
  with log.open('w') as stream:subprocess.run(command,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True,timeout=timeout,preexec_fn=limits)
  steps.append({'command':[str(x) for x in command],'seconds':time.monotonic()-before})
 for name in [*manifest['units'],'start.S']:
  src=directory/name;obj=src.with_suffix('.o')
  run([*cc,*flags,'-c',src,'-o',obj],src.with_suffix('.log'),120);objects.append(obj)
  print(f'{len(objects)}/{len(manifest["units"])+1} {name}',flush=True)
 run([*cc,*flags,'-nostartfiles','-no-pie',*objects,'-lm','-o',output],directory/'link.log',240)
 return {'compiler':subprocess.check_output([*cc,'--version'],text=True).splitlines()[0], 'flags':flags,'steps':steps,'seconds':time.monotonic()-started,'peak_child_rss_kib':resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss}
build.compile_c=compile_lto
out=root/'__dewycache__/compact-core/build-1792418000000000000'
build.build(root/'__dewycache__/compact-core/build-1792415673747283097',out,['gcc'])
p=out/'HOST_BUILD.json';m=json.loads(p.read_text());m['experiment']='O2 with sequential link-time optimization; scratch builder, not maintained release option';m['experiment_script']=str(Path(__file__).resolve());m['experiment_script_sha256']=build.identity(Path(__file__));p.write_text(json.dumps(m,indent=2)+'\n')

limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.
